chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kanasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Mention from the Greatness of Allah whatever you wish, but do not mention His Essence, for you do not mention anything from Him except that it is greater than it.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between discussing Allah's greatness and His Essence in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* encapsulates the Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), warning against *Tashbih* (anthropomorphism) by distinguishing between Allah's knowable attributes and His unknowable Essence (*Dhat*). It establishes that while human intellect can grasp divine qualities, any conceptualization remains finite and thus inferior to the infinite, incomparable reality of God. This principle serves as a foundational epistemological boundary in Shia theology, ensuring that worship and understanding remain rooted in humility rather than definitive definition.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. And with the same chain of transmission, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority `Ali ibn Ri’ab, on the authority of Durays al-Kanasi, that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said:
“Mention Allah’s Greatness as you wish, but do not discuss His Essence, as He is greater than anything you may mention.”
